messages:
anya: heads-up: after kernel-binning + kvcache-shard rollout we're seeing a subtle tail regression on host ingress. p95 moved up on many small payload streams. posting quick notes and a canary we ran with a host-proxy coalesce flag.
kevin: fyi i landed the coalesce toggle behind feature flag (host_proxy.coalesce_window_ms, host_proxy.coalesce_max_bytes). default is off. prototype: buffer writes up to 3KB or 1ms.
priya: can you paste the small profile? curious where time shifted.
anya: top CPU samples from the mini-bench (sorted):
```
12.4% token::tokenize
9.1% grpc::writev (syscall hotpath)
7.3% http::parse_headers
5.0% kvcache::lookup (hot-shard fallback)
3.8% kernel_selector::score_candidate
```
matt: interesting that tokenize is up too. any chance boundary shifts are causing extra work in tokenizer?
ben: i repro on bench VMs. new kernel hints shifted slice offsets -> increased fragment count into the framer -> more writev calls. GRPC writev syscall count up ~2.2x.
sara: i kicked off a tiny canary with coalesce enabled on pool-9 and a legacy-kernel-hint pool-10 for comparison. bench command used:
```
./tools/host-ingress-bench --clients 200 --payload 128 --rounds 500 --profile=out.pb
```
bench-bot: canary metrics (summary):
- pool-10 (legacy-hints): p95 ingress = 238ms, smallwrites = 0.13/wreq, kvcache_miss = 0.98%
- pool-9 (coalesce on): p95 ingress = 222ms, smallwrites = 0.08/wreq, kvcache_miss = 1.02%
- rollout baseline (no coalesce, new-hints): p95 ingress = 260ms, smallwrites = 0.29/wreq, kvcache_miss = 1.85%
anya: looks like coalesce reduces smallwrites and p95 without touching kernel selection. kvcache miss stayed ~same vs baseline, so it doesn't hide kvcache behavior.
kevin: good. impl note: coalesce is very cheap - we allocate a stack buffer inside host-proxy's write path, aggregate up to N frames or until timer fires, then emit single writev. added a feature toggle so we can enable/rollback quickly.
priya: do we have any downside? additional tail from waiting on coalesce window? we must tune to avoid increasing latency for larger payloads.
matt: we should A/B with 0.5ms, 1ms, 2ms windows and monitor p50/p95/p99. i'll add a dashboard template.
ben: also enable per-shard kvcache telemetry for the next few hours so we can see if misses correlate with particular shard/host. if coalesce masks the symptom for a while we still need to fix kernel hint alignment.
sara: rolled out 1ms coalesce to pool-9 canary. initial 30m snapshot: p95 dropped ~14% vs rollout baseline, smallwrite rate dropped ~72%. attaching pprof link: https://pprof.internal/6312350001/canary
anya: strong signal. proposal: enable coalesce as default in host-proxy for 2 weeks behind a kill-switch while we continue to iterate kernel hints (smaller diff) + kvcache per-shard metrics. rollback plan ready if any regression.
kevin: i'll prepare a small follow-up PR to expose window size via runtime config and add a kill-switch env var HOST_PROXY_COALESCE=false.
priya: agree to short-term default opt-in while we fix the root cause. let's target turning on for all hostpools in 48h if no regressions.
matt: adding A/B plan and dashboard panels: smallwrite rate, p95 ingress, kvcache_miss_by_shard. will share links.
bench-bot: note: remember to run the microbench after any kernel hint tweak: ./tools/mini-overhead-bench --payload-size 64 --rounds 2000 --profile=pprof.out
anya: thanks all. logging outcome here: coalesce reduces syscall fragmentation and immediate tail pain; next: fix kernel hint alignment & continue kvcache shard investigation. i'll open follow-up tickets for kernel-hint delta bisection and kvcache shard telemetry.
kevin: landed canary toggle and PR in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/host-proxy/pull/482
priya: great. keep notes in the ticket and let's sync tomorrow at 10 for roll plan. :calendar:
